title: Knowledge check: DOM Template Refs

questions.prompt: Which approach best matches “DOM Template Refs”?
options: Register a global listener on every update without cleanup.
Assume nextTick() runs before Vue’s queued DOM update.
Use lifecycle hooks when the component reaches the required phase, and remove timers, listeners, and subscriptions during cleanup.
Read a DOM element before it has mounted.
questions.answer_key: Use lifecycle hooks when the component reaches the required phase, and remove timers, listeners, and subscriptions during cleanup.
questions.explanation: This answer addresses DOM Template Refs directly. Verify the behavior in a small Vue 3 example and check the runtime requirements in the linked official reference.

questions.prompt: For “Referencing DOM elements”, which practice is most reliable?
options: nextTick() runs before Vue updates the DOM.
Place DOM-dependent work after mount and clean up listeners or subscriptions when they are no longer needed.
Use a template ref before the element is mounted.
Register duplicate global listeners on every update without cleanup.
questions.answer_key: Place DOM-dependent work after mount and clean up listeners or subscriptions when they are no longer needed.
questions.explanation: This practice supports the syllabus subtopic “Referencing DOM elements”. Check the expected result and a relevant boundary or failure case.

questions.prompt: A learner example for “DOM Template Refs” behaves unexpectedly. What should be checked first?
options: Reproduce the state or input change, inspect the relevant Vue binding or dependency, and compare the result with the expected output.
Change unrelated files until the page looks correct.
Disable error handling and assume the framework is at fault.
Trust a client-supplied success flag without checking behavior.
questions.answer_key: Reproduce the state or input change, inspect the relevant Vue binding or dependency, and compare the result with the expected output.
questions.explanation: Start with a small reproducible case. Inspect the element, reactive source, Console, and expected result before changing unrelated code.
